lead.headline: Three Big Countries Sit at One Table
lead.deck: Leaders of the US, China and Russia agreed a nuclear war must never happen.
body: Three leaders of very big countries met at one table this week. They were Donald Trump of the United States, Xi Jinping of China and Vladimir Putin of Russia. They met on November 19 in Shenzhen, a city in China.

At the end of their meeting, the three leaders signed what they called a declaration toward peace. In it, they said a nuclear war can never be won and must never be fought. Nuclear weapons are very powerful weapons.

But one big problem was left out. Russia has been fighting a war in Ukraine. The leaders did not agree how to end it, and their statement did not even mention it. No one from Ukraine was at the table.

world.headline: A Country Beats an Eye Sickness
world.deck: Eritrea, in East Africa, has stopped trachoma from being a big health problem.
body: Trachoma is a sickness of the eyes. It is caused by tiny germs called bacteria. It spreads when germs from one person's eyes or nose reach another person.
If a person catches it again and again, the eyelid can get scars. Then the eyelashes can turn inward, toward the eye. Over time, this can make a person blind, which means they cannot see.

That is why a big health group is cheering for Eritrea, a country in East Africa. On November 16, the World Health Organization, called WHO, said Eritrea has beaten trachoma as a public health problem. It is the 34th country in the world to do this.

How did Eritrea do it? It used a plan called SAFE. S is for surgery. A is for antibiotics, medicines that fight bacteria. F is for clean faces. E is for a better environment, like clean water and toilets.
Around the world, far fewer people need help with trachoma now. In 2002, about 1.5 billion people did. By November 2025, fewer than 100 million did.

us.headline: Hundreds of Glaciers Have Melted Away
us.deck: Scientists checked the ice on mountains in six western states.
body: A glacier is a giant sheet of ice that stays on a mountain all year. Scientists studied more than 1,300 glaciers in six states in the western United States.

They compared old records from the 1950s to the 1980s with pictures taken from planes and satellites around 2015. Nearly 400 glaciers have disappeared. The ones that are left have lost about one third of their ice.

Some mountains lost even more. In California's Sierra Nevada, the land covered by glaciers shrank by about 64 percent. In Wyoming's Wind River Range, it shrank by about 48 percent. Other glaciers last longer because steep rock walls shade them from the sun.

chart.title: GLACIER LAND LOST
chart.subtitle: Percent of glacier area gone
chart.caption: Both mountain areas lost about half or more of their glacier land.

us.why: Glaciers are like water towers. In hot, dry months, their melting ice keeps streams cold and flowing.

science_and_technology.headline: Lost Meerkats Find Their Way Home
science_and_technology.deck: Alone and far from their group, most meerkats walked straight back.
body: Meerkats are small animals that live in groups in the Kalahari Desert, in southern Africa. Scientists from the University of Zurich wondered something. Can one meerkat find its way home all alone?
To find out, they put GPS collars on meerkats. GPS tracks where something is. The scientists took one meerkat at a time 1.5 kilometres away and let it go. Then they followed it on foot.
They tried this 20 times. 18 of the 20 meerkats went straight back to their group or to the spot where they were caught. The other two may have been too stressed to move.
How did they do it? Each meerkat stood up on its back legs to look around. Then it walked in a straight line, stopping now and then to look again or to sniff for smells it knew.
science_and_technology.why: Meerkats live in groups, so scientists were surprised that each one seems to know the way by itself.
